Bioinformatics Resource Center - Rockefeller University" author: - "[http://rockefelleruniversity.github.io/responsible_use_of_AI_for_noncoders/](http://rockefelleruniversity.github.io/responsible_use_of_AI_for_noncoders/)" - "[brc@rockefeller.edu](mailto:brc@rockefeller.edu)" --- ::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"} # Responsible Use of AI for Non-Coders: Customizing Your LLM ::: ## Overview - [Skills](#skills) - [Connectors ](#connectors) - [Plugins](#plugins) - [Exercises](#time-for-an-exercise) # Customizing {background-color="#23373B" .center .middle} ## Customising your AI agent We have seen that we can guide how an AI agent acts by providing relevant files - * CLAUDE.md, Agents.md. * Memory.md. * RAG databases. ## Customising AI agent's abilities. We can also control how an agent acts when it wants to perform a certain task and/or undergo an action. To do this we can make use of SKILLs and/or MCP servers. SKILLs - Self contained markdown files describing tool use or computational protocol. MCP - API service allowing the use of specific functions. ## Built-in Slash commands {.smaller} Agent harnesses such as as Claude Code/Codex/Opencode have built in commands which we can use to control our sessions. The names differ between tools, but the ideas are the same. | What it does | Claude Code | Codex | opencode | |---|---|---|---| | Summarise the conversation to free up context | `/compact` | `/compact` | `/compact` | | Ask a quick side question without adding it to the conversation | `/btw` | `/side` (or `/btw`) | `/btw` | | Go back to an earlier point (conversation and/or files) | `/rewind` | `Esc Esc` (edit last message, fork from there) | `/undo`, `/redo` | | Plan first, change nothing until you approve | `/plan` | `/plan` | `Tab` (switch to Plan agent) | | Share or view outputs outside the terminal | `/artifacts` | `/app` (open in desktop app, which previews files) | `/share` (link to the session) | Type `/` in any of them to see the full list for your version. ::::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"} ::: notes Commands change between versions; checked November 2026. opencode's /undo and /redo need the project to be a git repository. Codex's /side opens a temporary side chat (/btw is an alias); opencode's built-in /btw is in recent versions, older ones need a plugin. ::: ::::: # SKILLs {#skills .center .middle background-color="#23373B"} ## What is a Skill A SKILL is a way for you to extend your AI agent's abilities with additional information such as a workflow and/or protocol. SKILLs are loaded on demand as required by the user using a "/" invocation or by the AI agent as it determines necessary. ## The Skill format Originally formalized by Anthropic, SKILLs follow a open format - [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io/specification) standard A SKILL is directory containing at a minimum a SKILL.md file. My_favourite_Skill/ ├── SKILL.md # Required: metadata + instructions ├── scripts/ # Optional: executable code ├── references/ # Optional: documentation ├── assets/ # Optional: templates, resources └── ... # Any additional files or directories # SKILL.md file {#skill-md .center .middle background-color="#23373B"} ## SKILL.md file - YAML header The required *SKILL.md* file needs a YAML header and must have the `name` and `description` fields. - **name:** can only contain lower case letters, numbers, and hypens (no hyphens at the beginning or end of the name) - **description:** max of 1024 characters outlining what this skill does, and when the model should use it. ```{.yaml filename="SKILL.md"} --- name: bioinformatics-skill description: What does this skill do? When should it be used? --- ``` ## SKILL.md file - Body section After the metadata header, the rest of the SKILL.md file is markdown-formatted text providing instructions to the model. This can take many forms, but it might include: - steps in a workflow - expected outputs - common problems to avoid - when to run scripts in the skills folder - recommended to keep below 500 lines (~5k tokens) - more details or code templates can be selectively read from the *references* or *assets* folders. ## Templates. When making reports it can be good to provide template files in the "references/" folder to allow for consistency in your reporting. Templates can be in any format but Markdown and Quarto formats provide an easily readable format for reports with code for plotting/visualisation including and citation management included. ## Good skill practice # SKILL management and installation {#skillmanagment .center .middle background-color="#23373B"} ## Skill scope The location of this folder will determine where that skill is available. - for global skills, with claude this will be located at *~/.claude/skills* - this will be slightly different for other models (e.g. *~/.codex/skills/*) - skills can also be limited to specific folders or projects. - a *.claude* or *.codex* directory can exist anywhere on your system, and your session will read any skill that exists in the path of that project. ## Public Skill repositories - [awesome-skills.com](https://awesome-skills.com/?tags=review) - [https://github.com/anthropics/skills](https://github.com/anthropics/skills) - [https://github.com/openai/plugins](https://github.com/openai/plugins) - [https://github.com/mattpocock/skills](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills) - [https://github.com/obra/superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) - [https://github.com/GoekeLab/awesome-genomic-skills](https://github.com/GoekeLab/awesome-genomic-skills): good resource for bioinformatics or science-focused skills ### Example skills - `grill-me` - `Docker` - `no slop` ### Skill creator - `/skill-creator` ## Connectors ### Loading connectors ### Connector repositories ## Plugins ### Plugin repositories ### BRC MCP ## Time for an exercise! Exercises on customizing your LLM can be found [here](../../exercises/exercises/Exercise_Customizing_exercise.html) ## Answers to exercise Answers can be found [here](../../exercises/answers/Exercise_Customizing_answers.html)
